title: Find the String with LCP
summary: Define the lcp matrix for a string of n lowercase English letters as an n x n grid where each lcp[i][j] represents the length of the longest common prefix between the substrings starting at i and j.
statement: Define the lcp matrix for a string of n lowercase English letters as an n x n grid where each lcp[i][j] represents the length of the longest common prefix between the substrings starting at i and j. Given an n x n lcp matrix, find the alphabetically smallest string that matches the lcp matrix. If no such string exists, return an empty string. A string a is lexicographically smaller than string b if, at the first differing position, a has a letter that precedes b in the alphabet.
constraints: lcp[i][j] must equal the common-prefix length of suffixes beginning at i and j.
Return the lexicographically smallest lowercase string realizing the matrix.
Return an empty string when the matrix is inconsistent or needs more than 26 character groups.
hints: A positive LCP means the two starting characters must be equal; zero means they differ.
Process the first unassigned position and give its entire positive-LCP group the next smallest letter.
After constructing characters, verify every matrix cell backward using the LCP recurrence.
Greedy first-occurrence labeling is lexicographically minimal, while full recurrence validation rejects all inconsistent equality lengths.
editorial: Greedy first-occurrence labeling is lexicographically minimal, while full recurrence validation rejects all inconsistent equality lengths.

tests.explanation: Positions sharing positive LCP form alternating a and b groups, producing abab.
No length-two string can have diagonal LCP values one, so the matrix is invalid.
